tagline: A capital city with a marine park 10 minutes off its jetty and the world's best diving on its far coast — all reached by open speedboat today.
summary: Kota Kinabalu is the gateway to two of Borneo's signature water assets: the Tunku Abdul Rahman Marine Park islands (Gaya, Manukan, Sapi) minutes off Jesselton Point, and the Semporna/Sipadan dive cluster on the east coast that is permit-rationed precisely because demand so far outstrips capacity. Today every transfer is an open, weather-exposed speedboat. Marine mobility here is about replacing a wet, bumpy, noisy bounce with a smooth, near-silent foiling arrival — using the jetties that already exist and protecting the very reefs tourists come to see.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Every transfer in both clusters is short and well inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope — TAR Park hops are 2–4 nm with near-continuous rotation potential, and the Semporna→Sipadan dive runs are ~15–20 nm.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta-LR's 2,000 nm hybrid range, with no charging-infrastructure dependency, is the answer for linking KK's west coast to the east-coast Semporna cluster (~280 nm around Borneo) and for liveaboard-style multi-day dive itineraries where shore power is absent.

competitive_landscape: The water today is entirely conventional open speedboats — TAR Park day-trip operators out of Jesselton Point, resort transfer boats, and dive-operator runs from Semporna. All diesel, all weather-exposed, none premium or foiling. The pain is consistent: wet, bumpy, noisy rides that punish guests, divers and reefs alike. With permit-limited Sipadan demand and 500k+ marine-park visitors, the flows are proven and undifferentiated — the opening is comfort, reliability and a clean low-wake footprint.
seasonality: Sabah's west coast (KK / TAR Park) is sheltered and navigable year-round. The east coast (Semporna/Sipadan) sees the northeast monsoon roughen seas roughly Nov–Feb, with Sipadan diving best Apr–Dec; the inter-monsoon brings short squalls. Foiling above the surface chop is precisely where the smoother, more reliable ride earns its premium during marginal-sea windows.
regulatory_note: TAR Marine Park is administered by Sabah Parks (conservation authority) with reef-protection rules that favour low-wake, low-emission, near-silent craft; transfers operate from Jesselton Point under the Marine Department Malaysia. The Sipadan cluster runs under Sabah Parks' strict daily diver-permit regime. An all-electric foiling fleet aligns directly with marine-park conservation mandates and reef-impact reduction.
